t.5.56.1: Then, on the peak of that mountain Mahendra, the mighty monkeys led by Hanumān attained the highest joy.
t.5.56.2: Then Jāmbavān, overjoyed, asked that great monkey, the son of the Wind, who was full of delight, for an account of how the mission had gone.
t.5.56.3: How was the queen seen by you, and how does she live there? And how has that ten-faced Daśānana, doer of cruel deeds, conducted himself toward her?
t.5.56.4: O great monkey, tell us all this truly. Having heard the facts, we shall then deliberate further on the decision as to what must be done.
t.5.56.6: Then, thus commanded by him, his body hair bristling with delight, he bowed his head to the divine Sītā and spoke in reply.
t.5.56.7: Right before your very eyes, longing for the southern shore of the ocean and with my mind wholly collected, I leapt into the sky from the summit of Mahendra.
t.5.56.5: Whatever matter is to be told there by us once we have gone, and whatever must be kept guarded there, that, self-possessed as you are, may you explain to us.
t.5.56.8: And as I was going, something terrible appeared before me, like the very form of an obstacle: I saw a golden, divine peak, exceedingly lovely.
t.5.56.9: He regarded that mountain, standing there and blocking the path, as an obstacle.
t.5.56.10: Having approached that divine golden mountain, the best of mountains, I resolved in my mind: "This must be split asunder by me."
t.5.56.11: And struck by me with my tail, the peak of that great mountain, radiant like the sun, shattered into a thousand pieces.
t.5.56.12: Understanding my resolve, that great mountain spoke sweet words to me, saying "O son," as though gladdening my mind.
t.5.56.13: Know me also to be your paternal uncle, the friend of Mātariśvan, renowned by the name Maināka and dwelling in the great ocean.
t.5.56.14: In olden times, O son, the best of mountains had wings, and they roamed the earth at will, causing harm on every side.
t.5.56.15: Having heard of the conduct of the mountains, the great Indra, the blessed chastiser of Pāka, cut off their wings by the thousands with his thunderbolt.
t.5.56.17: And I must abide in the service of Rāma, O subduer of foes; Rāma is the foremost of upholders of dharma, his valor equal to that of great Indra.
t.5.56.16: But I was rescued from that by your great-souled father, Māruta; then, dear child, I was cast by him into the great ocean.
t.5.56.19: And permitted to go by that great-souled Maināka, I summoned my utmost speed and set out upon the remainder of the journey.
t.5.56.18: When I had heard these words of the great-souled Maināka and had made known my mission to the mountain, my mind was roused and eager to press on.
t.5.56.20: Then for a very long time I sped swiftly along my path; then I saw the goddess Surasā, the mother of the Nāgas.
t.5.56.21: In the middle of the ocean that goddess spoke these words to me: 'O best of monkeys, you have been appointed by the immortals as my food. Therefore I shall devour you, for after a long time you have been ordained for me.'
t.5.56.22: Thus addressed by Surasā, I stood bowed down with joined palms, and, my face turning pale, I spoke these words.
t.5.56.23: The glorious Rāma, son of Daśaratha, scorcher of foes, entered the Daṇḍaka forest together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa and with Sītā.
t.5.56.24: His wife Sītā has been carried off by the evil-minded Rāvaṇa. At Rāma's command I shall go into her presence as his messenger.
t.5.56.25: O you who dwell within his realm, you ought to render help to Rāma.
t.5.56.26: Then, after seeing Maithilī and Rāma, whose deeds are untiring, I shall come back to your mouth; truth itself stands as my pledge.
t.5.56.27: Thus addressed by me, Surasā, who could take any form at will, said: "No one may pass beyond me; this is the boon granted to me."
t.5.56.28: Thus addressed by Surasā, I stretched myself out ten yojanas, and then in an instant I became half as much again in breadth.
t.5.56.29: And she opened wide her mouth to match my own dimensions; seeing that mouth gaping open, I made my body small.
t.5.56.31: Then the goddess Surasā, in her own form, spoke to me again: "O best of monkeys, gentle one, go as you please for the accomplishment of your purpose."
t.5.56.30: At that very moment I again became the size of a thumb, and swiftly flying into that mouth, I came out of it in an instant.
t.5.56.33: Then, praised by all beings with cries of "Well done, well done!", I leapt into the vast sky like Garuḍa.
t.5.56.32: Reunite Vaidehī with the great-souled Rāghava, and be happy, O mighty-armed one; I am pleased with you, O vānara.
t.5.56.34: My shadow was seized, yet I could see nothing at all. Then I, my speed gone, looking around in the ten directions, saw nothing there by which my motion had been taken away.
t.5.56.35: Then the thought arose in me: what kind of obstacle is this that has arisen in my going, where no form is seen?
t.5.56.36: Grieving, I cast my gaze downward, and then I saw a fearsome rākṣasī lying in the water.
t.5.56.37: And laughing with a great roar, that fearsome one calmly spoke to me these firm and inauspicious words.
t.5.56.38: Where will you go, O huge-bodied one? You are the food I have longed for in my hunger; satisfy my body, which has long been without nourishment.
t.5.56.39: Then, saying "Very well," I accepted her words, and I swelled my body until it was larger than the measure of her mouth.
t.5.56.41: Then, contracting my vast form in the space of an eye's blink, I seized her heart and flew up into the expanse of the sky.
t.5.56.40: And her huge and dreadful mouth kept widening to devour me, yet she did not perceive me, nor the change of form I had made.
t.5.56.42: Her heart cut through by me, that terrible one, huge as a mountain, fell into the salt sea with her arms flung loose.
t.5.56.44: Having slain her, and remembering once more the urgent task, I traveled a great distance and beheld the southern shore of the ocean, adorned with mountains, where stands that city Laṅkā.
t.5.56.43: I hear from the Siddhas who move through the sky, together with the Cāraṇas, that the terrible Rākṣasī Siṃhikā was swiftly slain by Hanumān.
t.5.56.45: When the sun had gone to its setting, I entered the city, the dwelling of the Rākṣasas, unnoticed by those Rākṣasas of terrible prowess.
t.5.56.46: There, having entered Rāvaṇa's inner apartments, I searched the whole night for the daughter of Janaka, yet I did not see that slender-waisted lady.
t.5.56.47: Then, not seeing Sītā in Rāvaṇa's dwelling, I fell into an ocean of grief and could perceive no farther shore.
t.5.56.48: And as I went on grieving, I saw a splendid palace garden enclosed by a long, extended wall of gold.
t.5.56.50: In the middle of the Aśoka grove stood a great śiṃśapā tree; climbing it, I saw a golden grove of plantain trees.
t.5.56.49: Leaping down from the rampart, I then beheld a place thick with many trees.
t.5.56.51: Not far from the śiṃśapā tree I see a lady of excellent complexion, dark and youthful, with eyes like lotus petals and a face wasted from fasting.
t.5.56.52: She was surrounded by hideous, cruel rākṣasīs who feed on flesh and blood, like a doe surrounded by tigresses.
t.5.56.53: Having seen that woman in such a state, the blameless wife of Rāma, I remained right there in the śiṃśapā tree, watching her.
t.5.56.54: Then, in the abode of Rāvaṇa, I hear a tumultuous sound, exceedingly deep, mingled with the jingling of girdles and anklets.
t.5.56.55: Then I, deeply agitated, drew in my own form, and I stayed in the dense śiṃśapā tree like a bird.
t.5.56.56: Then the wives of Rāvaṇa, and Rāvaṇa of great might himself, arrived at that place where Sītā was staying.
t.5.56.57: Then, seeing him, the lord of the hosts of rākṣasas, the fair-hipped Sītā drew in her thighs and, with her arms, covered her full breasts.
t.5.56.58: Daśagrīva, fallen prostrate with his head bowed low, said to that Sītā, who was in the deepest sorrow, "Think highly of me."
t.5.56.60: Having heard these words of that evil-minded Rāvaṇa, Sītā, supremely enraged, spoke an excellent reply.
t.5.56.59: If you, proud woman, in your arrogance do not welcome me, then after two months, Sītā, I shall drink your blood.
t.5.56.61: O vilest of rākṣasas, how is it that your tongue has not fallen off as you speak what should never be spoken to the wife of Rāma of boundless splendour, the daughter-in-law of Daśaratha, lord of the Ikṣvāku race?
t.5.56.62: What kind of valour is yours, O ignoble one, you who carried me off in my husband's absence and came away, O wicked one, unseen by that great-souled man?
t.5.56.64: Thus addressed with harsh words by Jānakī, the ten-faced one suddenly blazed up with anger, like a fire upon a funeral pyre.
t.5.56.63: You are not Rāma's equal; you are not fit even to be his servant. Rāghava is worthy of sacrifice, truthful in speech, and renowned in battle.
t.5.56.65: Opening wide his cruel eyes and raising his right fist, he set about to kill Maithilī; then a cry of "Alas, alas!" was raised by the women.
t.5.56.66: Springing up from the midst of the women, the chief wife of that evil-minded one, named Mandodarī, restrained him.
t.5.56.68: O lord, take your pleasure here together with the maidens of the Devas and Gandharvas, and with the maidens of the Yakṣas as well; what will you do with Sītā?
t.5.56.67: And he, tormented by desire, was addressed by her in sweet words: "What need have you of Sītā, O you whose valour equals that of great Indra? Take your pleasure with me today; Jānakī is not superior to me."
t.5.56.69: Then that mighty night-wanderer was swiftly raised up by those assembled women and led to his own dwelling.
t.5.56.70: When that Daśagrīva had gone, the rākṣasīs with misshapen faces threatened Sītā with cruel and exceedingly dreadful words.
t.5.56.71: Jānakī regarded their words as mere straw, and their threats, once they reached Sītā, were then rendered meaningless.
t.5.56.72: Their roaring having proved vain, the flesh-eating rākṣasīs, now helpless, reported to Rāvaṇa Sītā's great resolve.
t.5.56.73: Then all of them together, their hopes shattered and their efforts abandoned, surrounded her on every side and fell under the sway of sleep.
t.5.56.74: And when those women had fallen asleep, Sītā, devoted to the welfare of her husband, wretched and deeply sorrowful, lamented piteously and grieved bitterly.
t.5.56.76: And I devised a means for the purpose of speaking with Jānakī; then I placed foremost the lineage of the Ikṣvāku race.
t.5.56.75: And when I had seen Sītā's dreadful plight, such as it was, I paused and pondered, and my mind found no peace.
t.5.56.77: Having heard the words I had spoken, words honored by hosts of royal sages, the queen, her eyes veiled with tears, replied to me.
t.5.56.78: Who are you, O bull among monkeys? By whom were you sent, and how have you come here? And what is your bond of affection with Rāma? Please tell me that.
t.5.56.79: Having heard those words of hers, I too spoke these words: "O queen, the ally of Rāma, your husband, is the mighty lord of the monkeys named Sugrīva, valiant and of fearsome prowess."
t.5.56.80: Know me to be his servant Hanumān, who has come here. I have been sent to you by my master Rāma, whose deeds are accomplished without strain.
t.5.56.81: And this signet ring, as a token of recognition, the glorious Dāśarathi himself, that tiger among men, gave for you, O illustrious lady.
t.5.56.82: Therefore I wish to be commanded by you, O Devī: what shall I do? Shall I carry you to the side of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa? What is your reply?
t.5.56.83: Having heard this and understood it, Sītā, the delight of Janaka, said: "Let Rāghava destroy Rāvaṇa and take me away."
t.5.56.84: Bowing my head to the blameless, noble queen, I asked her for a token of recognition that would gladden the heart of Rāghava.
t.5.56.85: Thus addressed, the fair-hipped lady, deeply distressed, gave me that finest and most excellent of jewels, and with words she entrusted me with a message.
t.5.56.86: Then, with a collected mind, I bowed to that king's daughter and walked around her keeping her on my right, and set out from there to come here, my heart uplifted.
t.5.56.87: Then, having resolved it in her mind, she spoke again in reply: "O Hanūmān, you should relate my story to Rāghava."
t.5.56.88: Act in such a way that the two heroes, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, accompanied by Sugrīva, may come here without delay as soon as they have heard the news.
t.5.56.89: Should this turn out otherwise, my life lasts only two months; Kākutstha will not see me, and I die like one who has no protector.
t.5.56.90: Hearing those piteous words, anger came over me, and I saw the further task that remained to be done next.
t.5.56.91: Then my body grew until it resembled a mountain, and, eager for battle, I began to destroy that grove.
t.5.56.92: Then the rākṣasīs with misshapen faces, now awakened, gazed upon that shattered grove, its beasts and birds bewildered and terrified.
t.5.56.93: And having seen me in that grove, they gathered together from here and there, and, having come, they quickly reported it to Rāvaṇa.
t.5.56.94: O king, this impregnable grove of yours has been ravaged by a wicked-souled monkey who, O mighty one, did not know your valour.
t.5.56.95: O lord of kings, quickly command the slaying of that evil-minded one who acts against your wishes, so that he may go to his destruction.
t.5.56.96: Hearing that, the lord of the Rākṣasas dispatched the Rākṣasas called Kiṃkaras, exceedingly hard to conquer and obedient to the mind of Rāvaṇa.
t.5.56.97: Of those who bore spears and maces in their hands, eighty thousand were slain by me with an iron club in that part of the grove.
t.5.56.98: Those of them who were left alive after the slaughter went off with swift steps and reported to Rāvaṇa that the army had been destroyed by me.
t.5.56.99: Then a thought arose in me, and I mounted the temple palace.
t.5.56.100: Having once more slain with a pillar a hundred Rākṣasas stationed there, I in my fury destroyed that palace, which was the very ornament of Laṅkā.
t.5.56.101: Then he commanded Jambumālin, the son of Prahasta.
t.5.56.102: With a most dreadful iron club I strike down that rākṣasa, endowed with strength and skilled in battle, together with his followers.
t.5.56.103: Hearing that, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, sent forth the mighty sons of his ministers, accompanied by a force of foot-soldiers. With my iron club alone I send them all to the abode of Yama.
t.5.56.104: Hearing that the ministers' sons had been slain in battle, Rāvaṇa sent forth five valiant generals, leaders of the army, swift in their prowess. I slew every one of them together with their troops.
t.5.56.105: Then again Daśagrīva sent his son Akṣa, of mighty strength, into battle together with many rākṣasas.
t.5.56.106: That youthful prince, the son of Mandodarī, skilled in battle, who had suddenly leapt up into the sky, I seized by both feet; and whirling him, shield and sword and all, a hundred times around, I dashed him to pieces.
t.5.56.107: Hearing that Akṣa had been struck down, the ten-faced Rāvaṇa, greatly enraged, then commanded his second son, named Indrajit, mighty and wild with the frenzy of battle.
t.5.56.108: I too, having rendered his entire army and that bull among Rākṣasas bereft of strength in battle, attained supreme joy.
t.5.56.109: For this mighty-armed one of great strength was sent forth by Rāvaṇa with great confidence, together with heroes wild with frenzy.
t.5.56.110: He bound me with great swiftness by means of the Brāhma weapon, and then the Rākṣasas there bound me fast with ropes.
t.5.56.111: Seizing me, they led me into the presence of Rāvaṇa, and the evil-minded Rāvaṇa, having seen me, spoke to me.
t.5.56.112: And when I was questioned about my coming to Laṅkā and the slaying of the rākṣasas, I declared there that all of it had been done for Sītā's sake.
t.5.56.113: Longing to see her, O lord, I have come to your abode; I am the monkey Hanumān, the true-born son of Māruta.
t.5.56.114: Know me to be Rāma's messenger, a monkey, the minister of Sugrīva. I have come here into your presence on Rāma's errand as his envoy.
t.5.56.115: Hear also the message that I declare to you: O lord of the rākṣasas, the lord of the monkeys has addressed to you a well-considered speech, joined with dharma, artha and kāma, beneficial like wholesome food.
t.5.56.116: While I was dwelling on Mount Ṛṣyamūka, abounding in great trees, Rāghava, valiant in battle, came to be my friend.
t.5.56.117: By him it was told to me, O king: “My wife has been carried off by a demon; for the sake of my help in that matter, you should make a pact with me.”
t.5.56.118: The lord Rāghava, together with Lakṣmaṇa, made a pact of friendship, with fire as witness, with Sugrīva, whose kingdom had been seized by Vālin.
t.5.56.119: Having destroyed Vālin in battle with a single arrow, he made the great king lord of the leaping vānaras.
t.5.56.120: Help must be given to him by us here with our whole being; sent by him in accordance with dharma, I have come here into your presence.
t.5.56.121: Let Sītā be brought here quickly and handed over to Rāghava, before the heroic monkeys destroy your army.
t.5.56.122: For who did not know of old the might of the monkeys, who go into the presence of the gods when invited?
t.5.56.123: When I told him, "Thus does the king of the vānaras speak to you," he grew enraged and glared at me as if to burn me up with his eyes.
t.5.56.124: By that rākṣasa of savage deeds I was ordered to be put to death.
t.5.56.125: Then his brother, the wise Vibhīṣaṇa by name, entreated that king of the rākṣasas on my account.
t.5.56.126: Indeed, the killing of an envoy is not sanctioned in the treatises on kingship, O Rākṣasa; and the truth, just as it is, must be made known by an envoy who speaks for one's welfare.
t.5.56.128: Thus addressed by Vibhīṣaṇa, Rāvaṇa commanded those rākṣasas: "Let this very tail of his be set on fire this very day!"
t.5.56.127: Even for a very grave offence by an envoy, you of matchless valor, disfigurement is the punishment that has been seen; according to the śāstras, there is no slaying here.
t.5.56.129: Then, having heard his words, they wrapped my tail all around with strips of hemp bark and likewise with cotton cloths.
t.5.56.130: Then those rākṣasas of fierce valour, fully armed, set my tail ablaze, beating me with sticks and fists.
t.5.56.131: Though I am bound with many nooses and held fast by the rākṣasas, no pain at all would befall me, since I wish to see the city by day.
t.5.56.132: Then those valiant rākṣasas, having come to the city gate, proclaimed me along the royal road, bound and enveloped in fire.
t.5.56.133: Then, contracting once more my own very great form and freeing myself from that bond, I stood again restored to my natural state.
t.5.56.135: And with my blazing tail, unperturbed, I burned that city with its watchtowers and gateways, as the fire at the end of an age burns all creatures.
t.5.56.134: Seizing an iron bar, I slew those Rākṣasas; then I leapt swiftly onto the gate of that city.
t.5.56.136: And having burned Laṅkā, a fear came over me once more: in burning Laṅkā, I have surely burned Sītā as well; there is no doubt.
t.5.56.137: Then I heard the auspiciously worded speech of the Cāraṇas, who were speaking in wonder of the news: "Jānakī has not been burned!"
t.5.56.138: Then, when I had heard that wondrous utterance, a resolve arose in me; Vaidehī was seen once more, and I was again sent off by her.
t.5.56.139: By the power of Rāghava and by your own splendour, and for the sake of Sugrīva's cause, all this has been accomplished by me.
t.5.56.140: All this has been duly accomplished by me there. Whatever remains here that has not been done, let all of that be done.
